# Find the maximum value in the 'Depot_inter' column
max_depot_value = df_time_series['Depot_inter'].max()

# Find the index of the maximum value
max_depot_index = df_time_series['Depot_inter'].idxmax()

# Find the corresponding CE value
peak_ce = df_time_series.loc[max_depot_index, 'CE']

# Convert the CE value to a century
peak_century = (peak_ce // 100) + 1

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Plot the 'Depot_inter' values over time
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(df_time_series['CE'], df_time_series['Depot_inter'], label='Depot Interpolated')
plt.xlabel('CE (Common Era)')
plt.ylabel('Depot Interpolated Z Values')
plt.title('Depot Interpolated Z Values Over Time')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Plot the 'Depot' values over time
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(df_time_series['CE'], df_time_series['Depot'], label='Depot Original')
plt.xlabel('CE (Common Era)')
plt.ylabel('Depot Original Z Values')
plt.title('Depot Original Z Values Over Time')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Calculate a rolling mean of the 'Depot_inter' values with a window size of 100 years
df_time_series['Depot_inter_rolling'] = df_time_series['Depot_inter'].rolling(window=100).mean()

# Find the maximum value in the rolling mean
max_rolling_depot_value = df_time_series['Depot_inter_rolling'].max()

# Find the index of the maximum value in the rolling mean
max_rolling_depot_index = df_time_series['Depot_inter_rolling'].idxmax()

# Find the corresponding CE value
peak_rolling_ce = df_time_series.loc[max_rolling_depot_index, 'CE']

# Convert the CE value to a century
peak_rolling_century = (peak_rolling_ce // 100) + 1

peak_rolling_century
